basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and progressive neurologic dysfunction define the umbrella; hepatic failure and immunodeficiency are subtype-dependent.
Curariform toxicity blocks neuromuscular transmission; respiratory paralysis reflects neuromuscular dysfunction rather than direct lung damage.
Bardet-Biedl phenotype includes retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; renal abnormalities occur in roughly 50%; common cognitive impairment omitted by cap.
Malignant germ cell tumor originating in the central nervous system.
Congenital ocular motor dysfunction with nystagmus and reduced visual acuity; no independent neurologic disease established.
Congenital alopecia and keratoderma define the disorder; cataracts with visual impairment and joint stiffness each occur in 80–99%.
Defined by variably penetrant polycystic kidney and/or liver disease; a glycosylation-related gene alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Sensory ganglion disease directly damages peripheral sensory neurons; non-paraneoplastic status does not establish an immune mechanism.
Skeletal dysplasia defines 3M syndrome; hypospadias, a urethral malformation within the renal axis, is reported in 10/11 patients.
Neurodevelopmental and structural eye defects define it; congenital heart (~50%) and kidney (~30%) defects are common; sparse hearing/skeletal findings omitted by cap.
B-cell developmental deficiency with agammaglobulinemia and reduced B-cell counts in 4/4; recurrent otitis is a separately diagnosed infection.
Cerebellar degeneration defines the disorder; cataracts directly affect the eyes in 2/2 reported patients.
Urothelial neoplasm originating in the ureter.
Defined hepatic vascular disease with blood-filled sinusoidal cavities affecting liver tissue.
Neoplasm of the hair follicle infundibulum, a cutaneous appendage.
Inherited ocular refractive and growth disorder causing myopia.
Inherited atrial rhythm disorder; thromboembolic stroke occurred in 2/10 and is a separately diagnosed complication.
Lymphatic vascular malformation with ASD in 6/11; pleural lymph leakage causes chylothorax in 6/10; anemia in 3/10 lacks clear direct blood pathology.
Lysosomal storage disorder causing progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients over the course.
Gastrointestinal stromal tumor originating in the colon or rectum.
Motor neuron disease with overlapping intrinsic MATR3 myopathy: rimmed vacuoles in 5/6 and abnormal muscle nuclei in 3/6; respiratory weakness is neuromuscular.
Severe cerebellar and neurodevelopmental dysfunction; persistent strabismus affects 3/4 (75%); isolated clinodactyly does not establish locomotor impairment.
Peripheral arterial narrowing or obstruction causes deficient limb perfusion; tissue infarction is not established as a common defining feature.
Aplasia of female reproductive tract structures; associated urinary or skeletal syndromes are not inherent to this umbrella concept.
Squamous cell carcinoma originating in the rectum.
